facets.title: Exact S01 composite package and S02 typed task compatibility
facets.caveat: A model label without exact weights, tokenizer, adapters and task input/output constraints is not verified support.

facets.title: M07 observed device topology, framework, driver and precision exposure
facets.caveat: Self-reported GPU model names or cached device descriptions are not verified exact current runtime evidence.

facets.title: Actual future M08 bounded protocol, fixture, correctness and qualification
facets.caveat: A prospective protocol or synthetic CPU hash result is not an independent provider/GPU model compatibility benchmark.

facets.title: Candidate precision, compiled graph, attention kernels and provider operator availability
facets.caveat: Claimed backend/precision support cannot authorize installing or importing unreviewed M13/M16/M17 custom code.

facets.title: Future VRAM peaks, fragmentation, thermal state, sustained tests and I/O load
facets.caveat: One burst sample or a claimed model fit must not become a current M09 complete-member lease or OOM guarantee.

facets.title: Evidence conflicts, staleness, drift, aborts, unknown telemetry and revoked facts
facets.caveat: Stale device/runtime identity and UNKNOWN hardware readings remain non-positive qualification evidence.

facets.title: Tenant-scoped package rights, trusted operators, OS permissions and revocation
facets.caveat: Model or hardware compatibility never grants commercial use, foreign tenant access, network calls or process rights.

facets.title: Separate M01 acceptance, M02 master, M09 lease and M11/M12 dispatch gates
facets.caveat: Quality veto, production approval, live resource grants and worker ACK are independent gates outside M14.

alternatives.title: Vendor GPU and model tag matrix
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cheap discovery only: mutable GPU names and package aliases omit exact firmware, driver, typed task, permissions and invalidation.

alternatives.title: Typed model-package, task, M07 snapshot and protocol tuple
alternatives.tradeoffs: Explicit comparison boundaries but still unverified until a real qualified owner, exact M08 result and per-tenant rights exist.

alternatives.title: Revisioned model/task/device/backend evidence and invalidation graph
alternatives.tradeoffs: Better conflict and revocation lineage but needs independent signed issuers and transparent M07/M08 semantics, not a guessed score.

alternatives.title: Future qualified at-use hardware-compatibility evidence receipt
alternatives.tradeoffs: Cannot exist here without actual M08 representative measurement, independent M14/M18/M54 approval and M09/M11/M12 authority separation.

questions.question: How must exact S01 package closure and typed S02 task dimensions jointly identify the subject of a future hardware support claim?
What precise M07 hardware identity, device topology, current driver, runtime and normalized precision facts must be present before a model can be tested?
Which hardware capability declarations are merely self-reported rather than confirmed by independent capable and correctly scoped M07 probes?
How should a future real M08 protocol bind exact model task/fixture, M07 host, safety budget and authenticated permission to measure?
Which actual model correctness and M01 fidelity evidence must precede any future accuracy or speed comparison for a target workload?
What declared FP8/FP16/BF16 precision representations, accumulation and operator compatibility require separate conformance evidence?
How can compiled attention kernels, graph breaks and custom operators remain unsupported claims until separate M13/M16/M18 trust owners qualify them?
Which initial and peak VRAM allocations, host fallback and fragmentation data are required before calling an exact workload memory-compatible?
How can unknown thermal telemetry, abort, repeated resets and competing-process interference prevent false sustained-reliability claims?
What is the owner-approved distinction between one supported burst, a repeated representative run and production reliability for each workload?
Which storage, I/O, transfer and CPU/GPU overlap measurements may be described without authorizing a runtime scheduler or file-system access?
What package/environment incompatibilities require an INCOMPARABLE result rather than a numeric score or silent default provider fallback?
How should differing M07 runtime versions, firmware, driver and device revisions revoke inherited historical compatibility labels?
Which exact evidence clock, provenance, freshness, conflict and withdrawal markers must fail closed before any real qualification is published?
How must an M09 lease, member set, owner receipt and lifecycle event remain separate from a declared model memory-fit hint?
What independent M11 process-owner ACK, M12 attempt fence and M60 OS authority is required beyond future M14 hardware evidence?
Which rights, tenant scope, executable package trust and revoked license facts are required before even a physically compatible model may be used?
How should M01 unresolved fatal quality defects and the accepted M02 master prevent an empirically faster model from being silently promoted?
Which low-VRAM/CPU-only fallback declarations must be distinguished from representative empirical support and actual platform permissions?
How do multi-device topology, peer accessibility and driver interoperability affect uncertainty without claiming cross-device production support?
Which original source-owner attestation and independent M18/M54 supply/rights review must precede a real M14 hardware qualification receipt?
Which future S05 invalidation and drift conditions should retire a once-qualified host/model binding while preserving historical source provenance?

negativeScenarios.trigger: Vendor declares a GPU model supported, but the current M07 runtime has conflicting driver and missing framework exposure.
One model alias is pinned while its tokenizer or adapter changes and old hardware compatibility results are reused.
A source-only M08 protocol is promoted to a real GPU model qualification without actual probe or permission receipts.
A CPU hash microbenchmark is used to assert GPU diffusion performance and a new typed image workflow's compatibility.
A vendor FP8 badge is accepted while the actual host arithmetic format, conversion and accumulation evidence is unknown.
A compiled attention backend imports an untrusted extension while M13/M16/M18 owners and native execution rights are absent.
A single short low-VRAM generation run is treated as stable sustained use despite unknown fragmentation and memory peaks.
Unknown thermal readings and aborted runs are relabeled as valid representative sustained reliability measurements.
A speculative CPU/GPU overlap design is treated as authorization for storage operations, IO scheduling and worker processes.
An incompatible firmware/runtime revision is silently mapped to a different benchmark and ranked by numerical speed.
A stale compatibility receipt remains positive after original device evidence expiry, revocation or conflicting topology.
A model task's measured memory hint is converted into a live M09 all-member resource lease with no actual owner approval.
A purported model-card hardware PASS is used to launch an M11 worker despite absent M12 attempt fence and OS grant.
A foreign tenant reuses another tenant's qualified model evidence and rights after their source permission expires.
A faster provider result suppresses a documented fatal M01 defect and overwrites the previously accepted M02 master.
A text-only CPU result is presented as representative support for a low-VRAM temporal video workload on an unseen GPU.
A multi-GPU peer-access hint claims complete tested interoperability when only one directional link had fresh evidence.
A previously source-qualified package and device label survives original signature revocation and S05 model drift.
